Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom uptime & latency SLA addendum for Pinebrook

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and prefix caching features. We're moving toward signature on the MSA + SOW, but procurement needs a short SLA addendum that clarifies uptime and latency commitments for the Dedicated environment we plan to reserve.

High level asks from our side:
- Minimum monthly uptime for Dedicated capacity (we currently ask for 99.95% in our contracts)
- P99 inference latency target for synchronous text-generation requests (we'd like 300–400ms for our primary tenant under baseline load)
- Credit calculation and remediation steps when targets aren't met

I've attached the current SOW (Pinebrook_SOW_v4.pdf) and a short procurement template showing the language our legal team prefers. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short addendum (1–2 pages) with precise order form changes and credit table? If you could send a draft we can share with our legal and SRE teams that would speed review.

Thanks,
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Cloud Architecture — Pinebrook Health
procurement@pinebrookhealth.com
(415) 555-0192

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the SOW. Happy to draft an addendum. Quick clarifying questions so we shape the language correctly:

1) When you say "Dedicated capacity" — is the expectation for reserved GPU pools (Dedicated) with SLA applied per order form, or do you expect the same wording to apply if you run in our Hosted plan with pinned capacity?
2) Is the 300–400ms P99 target for single-request generation at short sequences (~512 tokens) or for your 1–3 prompt workloads? Having target sequence lengths helps us map to our performance grading table.
3) Any specific credit multiplier your legal team expects (e.g., 10% service credit per 0.1% below uptime)?

I'll loop in Laura (contracts) and Tessa (SRE/operational SLAs) to confirm what we can commit to and to prepare a calibrated credit table. Proposed timeline: I can get a draft addendum and an order-form redline to you by EOD Thursday. Would a short call on Thursday morning to walk through the table help?

—Marcus

Folks — forwarding Pinebrook's note (see below). They want a concise addendum and a revised order form. My proposed approach:

- Offer a scoped SLA Addendum (Addendum A) that applies only to Redwood Dedicated capacity ordered on the related order form. Addendum will not apply to hosted shared tenancy.
- Uptime commitment: 99.95% monthly availability of the Dedicated pool for their tenant. Exceptions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure as usual.
- Latency commitment: P99 inference latency <= 350ms for synchronous generation requests at sequence lengths up to 768 tokens under their committed baseline throughput (we'll request their baseline rps; draft will say "as measured by Redwood telemetry under normal operating conditions").
- Credits: tiered service credit table: 10% credit for monthly uptime between 99.90%–99.95%, 25% for 99.50%–99.90%, 50% for <99.50%. Cap at 100% of monthly invoice for the service.
- Operational remedies: 72-hour remediation plan, root cause report within 10 business days, can escalate to a dedicated technical review.

Open items for legal/ops: 1) confirm credit caps; 2) confirm latency measurement methodology and exclusion windows (e.g., deploys, warm-up, burst overloads); 3) finalize order-form language to tie the addendum to a specific order number.

Thoughts? If you approve I will prepare a redline and a clean addendum PDF to send to Pinebrook.

—Marcus

Marcus — good framing. A few redline suggestions from contracts:

- Make explicit that the SLA applies only when Pinebrook has a Reserved/Dedicated order form in effect. Add a definition block for "Dedicated Environment" referencing order form id.
- For credits, legal prefers a clearer discrete table (we'll produce) but wants to limit payouts to a single monthly invoice for the Redwood service (not to exceed 100%). Keep your tiered approach but change the 10% band to be 5% for 99.90%–99.95% to reduce exposure.
- Latency measurement: request explicit reference to Redwood's telemetry and include an exclusion for known scheduled maintenance windows and customer-induced overloads. Also add a clause allowing Redwood to propose mitigations (e.g., burst capacity) before crediting.

Operational note for Tessa: please confirm whether the 350ms P99 target for sequences up to 768 tokens is realistic for the Dedicated GPU types we're pricing (we might have to specify a model family or instance class).

I'll prepare a redline doc (proposed-orderform-changes.docx) and a clean addendum (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Pinebrook_v1.pdf) for Marcus to send. Approve that we limit applicability to the specific order number and that all credits are applied as service credits on future invoices.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Hi Daniel — attaching a short draft addendum (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Pinebrook_v1.pdf) and a redline of the order form (proposed-orderform-changes.docx) that implement the items we discussed. High level summary below.

Summary of proposed commitments (applies only to Dedicated capacity on the attached order form):
- Monthly Availability: 99.95% availability of the Dedicated pool (excludes scheduled maintenance and force majeure).
- Latency: P99 inference latency <= 350ms for synchronous generation requests at sequence lengths up to 768 tokens, measured by Redwood telemetry under normal operating conditions and the customer's committed baseline throughput. Exclusions for burst overload and scheduled deploys.
- Credits: 5% service credit for uptime between 99.90%–99.95%; 25% credit for 99.50%–99.90%; 50% credit for <99.50%. Credits applied to future invoices; cap at 100% of the monthly invoice.
- Remedy process: 72-hour remediation window, root cause analysis within 10 business days, escalation path to a technical review board as needed.

Next steps I propose:
1) If this draft looks directionally correct, sign a short mutual NDA for order-form redlines (if needed) and then we can produce a DocuSign envelope for the addendum and order form.
2) If you want, Tessa can host a 30-min technical call to align measurement methodology and the baseline throughput assumptions.

I copied Laura and Tessa on this email — they will be the point people on the contract and operational details respectively. Please let me know any immediate changes; otherwise I will send a DocuSign link for the addendum + order form by end of day Monday.

Best,
Marcus Lin
